answer.worked:

content.prompt: Grandma Betty spent $\$100$ buying Christmas presents and cards for friends and relatives in one shop and bought altogether 100 items. She bought books for $\$10$ each, pens for $\$2$ each and cards for 50 cents each. How many of each did she buy? There are two possible answers.

answer.short: 1 book, 27 pens and 72 cards; or 4 books, 8 pens and 88 cards.
answer.worked:
Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be the numbers of books, pens and cards respectively.
$$\begin{align*}x+y+z&=100 &&(1)\\10x+2y+0.5z&=100 &&(2)\\z&=100-x-y &&(3)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (3) into (2).
$$\begin{align*}10x+2y+0.5(100-x-y)&=100\\9.5x+1.5y+50&=100\\9.5x+1.5y&=50\\19x+3y&=100\end{align*}$$
Since the counts are non-negative whole numbers, try $x=0,1,2,3,4,5$. Only $x=1$ and $x=4$ give whole-number values of $y$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=1:& y&=\frac{100-19}{3}=27,& z&=100-1-27=72\\x&=4:& y&=\frac{100-76}{3}=8,& z&=100-4-8=88\end{align*}$$
Therefore she bought 1 book, 27 pens and 72 cards; or 4 books, 8 pens and 88 cards.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{(x-1)(x+1)}&=\frac{a}{x-1}+\frac{b}{x+1}\\6&=a(x+1)+b(x-1)\\6&=x(a+b)+(a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=0\quad(1)\\a-b&=6\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and (2):
$$\begin{align*}2a&=6\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=3$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}3+b&=0\\b&=-3\\\frac{6}{(x-1)(x+1)}&=\frac{3}{x-1}-\frac{3}{x+1}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{7}{(x+2)(2x-3)}&=\frac{a}{x+2}+\frac{b}{2x-3}\\7&=a(2x-3)+b(x+2)\\7&=x(2a+b)+(-3a+2b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}2a+b&=0\quad(1)\\-3a+2b&=7\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Twice (1) minus (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=-7\\a&=-1\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=-1$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}-2+b&=0\\b&=2\\\frac{7}{(x+2)(2x-3)}&=-\frac{1}{x+2}+\frac{2}{2x-3}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{-5}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}&=\frac{a}{2x-1}+\frac{b}{3x+1}\\-5&=a(3x+1)+b(2x-1)\\-5&=x(3a+2b)+(a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}3a+2b&=0\quad(1)\\a-b&=-5\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and twice (2):
$$\begin{align*}5a&=-10\\a&=-2\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=-2$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}-2-b&=-5\\b&=3\\\frac{-5}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}&=-\frac{2}{2x-1}+\frac{3}{3x+1}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{9x+4}{(3x-1)(x+2)}&=\frac{a}{3x-1}+\frac{b}{x+2}\\9x+4&=a(x+2)+b(3x-1)\\9x+4&=x(a+3b)+(2a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+3b&=9\quad(1)\\2a-b&=4\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and three times (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=21\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=3$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}6-b&=4\\b&=2\\\frac{9x+4}{(3x-1)(x+2)}&=\frac{3}{3x-1}+\frac{2}{x+2}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x-1}{(x+3)(x-4)}&=\frac{a}{x+3}+\frac{b}{x-4}\\2x-1&=a(x-4)+b(x+3)\\2x-1&=x(a+b)+(-4a+3b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=2\quad(1)\\-4a+3b&=-1\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Three times (1) minus (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=7\\a&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=1$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}1+b&=2\\b&=1\\\frac{2x-1}{(x+3)(x-4)}&=\frac{1}{x+3}+\frac{1}{x-4}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1-x}{(2x-1)(4-x)}&=\frac{a}{2x-1}+\frac{b}{4-x}\\1-x&=a(4-x)+b(2x-1)\\1-x&=x(-a+2b)+(4a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}-a+2b&=-1\quad(1)\\4a-b&=1\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and twice (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=1\\a&=\frac17\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=\frac17$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}\frac47-b&=1\\b&=-\frac37\\\frac{1-x}{(2x-1)(4-x)}&=\frac{1}{7(2x-1)}-\frac{3}{7(4-x)}\end{align*}$$

4x + 5y = 8  (2)
1. (1) × 4 → 12x − 8y = 116  (3)

3. y = −4

entries.description: Given that (ax + b)² + c = 4x² − 4x + 2 for all x, find a, b and c.
Hence find all values of k for which 4x² − 4x + 2 = k has real solutions.

entries.expectedAnswer:
4x² − 4x + 2 = (2x − 1)² + 1
So for 4x² − 4x + 2 = k
(2x − 1)² + 1 = k
(2x − 1)² = k − 1
For real solutions, you must be able to square root the RHS; i.e:
k − 1 ≥ 0
k ≥ 1
You can also solve this using the discriminant
